names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 26 decembrie, «Sfântul Mucenic Eftimie, Episcopul Sardelor», with the rank and the see left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 26 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιος Ευθύμιος ο Ομολογητής, επίσκοπος Σάρδεων», with the rank word, the by-name and the see left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s fourth heading for 26. децембар ст. ст., „Свети Јевтимије Исповедник, епископ сардијски.“ — «Свети» is “saint” and not a rank, «Исповедник» is the rank `confessor` and «епископ» the rank `bishop`, both of which the folder already carries, and «сардијски» is the see, which §6 keeps out of a stored form and which the folder carries in its `office` and its display name. So the bare forename is what is left, and that is a reading rather than a regex: the see is the one thing here that would have told him apart. MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN, AND IT LANDS ON ANOTHER FOLDER: `euthymius-of-dimitsana` already holds the identical Serbian string, so the two-member fold key «јевтимије» is declared in the same commit with both holders read. The corpus’s four other Euthymii carry two-word Serbian forms — «Јевтимије Велики», «Јевтимије Иверски», «Јевтимије Нови», «Јевтимије Дохијарски» — which the fold key sorts as two words and which therefore reach neither this string nor each other.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 26 decembrie — «Sfântul Mucenic Eftimie, Episcopul Sardelor»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 26ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιος Ευθύμιος ο Ομολογητής, επίσκοπος Σάρδεων»

attestations.note: The life page `/2795/` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 26 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps for the Romanian, and it is the same man, the confessor bishop of Sardis beaten to death for the icons. What the page prints for a life is one long quotation from S. Eustratiades's Hagiology, in Greek of the last century, and everything in the upgrade comes out of it. **The page's head and the passage it quotes do not agree about when he died.** The head gives «(; - 840)» and is the only year of death on the page; the narrative, however, ends with his recall by Michael the Stammerer, whose reign it dates 820 to 829, his anathema spoken to the emperor's face, his exile to Akritas and his death eight days after the beating. The `dates` drafted take the head's year with `basis` traditional, and the note records the reign the narrative ends in. Two other things to read as the page's and not as corrections: it calls the Leo of 813 to 820 «Λέοντος τοῦ Ἰσαύρου», which those years do not fit, and it has his first exile to the island of Παττάλαρα on a charge that he had tonsured a girl whom a senior official wanted to marry. The skull of the saint is at the church of his name at Keratsini of Piraeus, which is not drafted; Lykaonia, Alexandria, Sardis, Nicaea, Assos by Adramyttion and Akritas are named and no coordinate is proposed. No hymn is printed on the Greek page, and the folder's Romanian troparion is untouched. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 08.01.2026 (26. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети Јевтимије Исповедник, епископ сардијски.“

attestations.note: The day’s fourth entry, and three sentences is the whole of it. Identified past any doubt and on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek already keep him: the heading gives both the grade and the see — «Исповедник», confessor, and «епископ сардијски», bishop of Sardis — and the body gives the Seventh Ecumenical Council, the thirty years of exile for the honouring of icons, and the scourging with ox sinews under the iconoclast emperor Theophilus. THE YEAR AGREES EXACTLY and `dates` is therefore untouched: «мученички сконча 840. године» against the flat 840 the folder already holds off saint.gr. `types` untouched and all four already there: `bishop`, `hierarch`, `confessor`, `martyr`, which is exactly what this heading and this body would read to. `office` untouched: Bishop of Sardis. WHAT THE ENTRY ADDS, and goes into the life: that he was PRESENT AT THE SEVENTH ECUMENICAL COUNCIL, which is a fact of his career the folder’s existing life does not carry; that the exile was «око тридесет година», about thirty years, which is a span of years and is written in no field; that the instrument was «воловским жилама», ox sinews; and that he received the crown of glory in heaven. No `related`: the entry names no saint at all, and Theophilus is a persecutor and not a companion — the folder’s three existing rows, to `nicetas-of-medikion`, `theophylact-of-nicomedia` and `eutychius-kachur`, predate this reading, stand untouched, and the new paragraph deliberately names none of them. No `locations`. The Serbian form is the heading’s forename with the rank and the see stripped; it lands on `euthymius-of-dimitsana`, which already holds the identical string, so the two-member fold key «јевтимије» is declared in `scripts/corpus-gate.mjs` in this same commit with both holders read. The Prologue prints no hymn (8 October 2026).

hymns.text: Îndreptător credinţei şi chip blândeţelor, învăţător înfrânării te-a arătat pe tine, turmei tale, adevărul lucrurilor. Pentru aceasta ai dobândit cu smerenia cele înalte şi cu sărăcia cele bogate; Părinte Ierarhe Eftimie, roagă pe Hristos Dumnezeu să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Ierarh Eftimie Mărturisitorul, Episcopul Sardei, glasul 4 (the common of a hierarch, printed with his name in it)

english.text: The truth of things has shown you to your flock a rule of faith, an image of gentleness and a teacher of continence. Therefore you have gained the heights by humility and riches by poverty. Father and hierarch Euthymius, pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

death.note: saint.gr's head for the page gives «Αγιος Ευθυμιος ο Ομολογητης, Επισκοπος Σαρδεων (; - 840)», and it is the only year of death the page carries. The Eustratiades passage the same page quotes ends his life under Michael the Stammerer, «(820 - 829 μ.Χ.)», who recalled him from exile and then exiled him to Akritas, where he died «ὀκτὼ ἡμέρας μετὰ τὴν ἄθλησιν»; that is recorded here and not reconciled with 840. No year of birth is given: the passage says only that he flourished under Constantine and Irene, «(780 - 797 μ.Χ.)», was born in Lykaonia and studied at Alexandria. The folder held no `dates` before this.
